info.title: Machines API
info.description: This site hosts documentation generated from the Fly.io Machines API OpenAPI specification. Visit our complete [Machines API docs](https://fly.io/docs/machines/api/) for how to get started, more information about each endpoint, parameter descriptions, and examples.

get.description: List all Machines associated with a specific app, with optional filters for including deleted Machines and filtering by region.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: comma separated list of states to filter (created, started, stopped, suspended)

parameters.name: summary
parameters.description: Only return summary info about machines (omit config, checks, events, host_status, nonce, etc.)

parameters.name: metadata.{key}
parameters.description: Filter by a machine metadata key and exact value. Replace {key} with the metadata key, for example metadata.foo=bar. Specify multiple metadata filters to require all matches.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Value of the fly-next-cursor response header from the previous page. Requires limit.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of machines to fetch (must be between 1 and 1000). Providing a limit enables pagination. This limit is advisory; responses may be shorter, or even empty, even when more machines remain.

fly-next-cursor.description: Pagination cursor for the next page. Absent when no more machines remain. Cursor expires 30 minutes after the first page was requested.

get.description: List all volumes associated with a specific app.

parameters.name: summary
parameters.description: Only return summary info about volumes (omit blocks, block size, etc)

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Value of the fly-next-cursor response header from the previous page. Requires limit.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of volumes to fetch (must be between 1 and 1000). Providing a limit enables pagination. This limit is advisory; responses may be shorter, or even empty, even when more volumes remain.

fly-next-cursor.description: Pagination cursor for the next page. Absent when no more volumes remain. Cursor expires 30 minutes after the first page was requested.

name.description:
Name of the check: the key of a top-level check in `config.checks`, or
`servicecheck-<index>-<type>-<internal_port>` for a check defined in a service.

output.description: Output of the most recent check run, such as an error message.

updated_at.description: When the check's status was last updated.

details.description: Deprecated: details about some errors. Do not rely on its contents.

error.description:
Human-readable description of the error. Its wording may change; use `status` to tell
errors apart.

status.description:
Machine-readable error code, set for some errors, such as `insufficient_capacity`,
`volume_placement_capacity`, `name_taken`, `exec_request_too_large`, or
`exec_output_too_large`.

registry.description: Registry host of the image, such as `registry.fly.io`.

repository.description: Repository of the image within the registry, such as `library/nginx`.

tag.description: Tag the image was referenced by, if any.

checks.description:
Status of each health check: the Machine's top-level `checks` and its services'
checks.

config.description:
The Machine's configuration, as provided when it was created or last updated, with
`metadata` and `mounts` reflecting their current values. Null when the host is not
reachable (`host_status` is not `ok`) or `summary=true` was requested; see
`incomplete_config`.

cordoned.description:
Whether the Machine is cordoned, meaning Fly Proxy does not route requests to it. See
the Cordon Machine endpoint.

events.description:
Up to 5 of the most recent events of the current Machine version, newest first. Use
the List Events endpoint for more.

host_features.description:
Features of the Machine's host, for comparison with `config.guest.required_host_features`.
Only returned when the request sets the `fly-include-host-features: true` header.

host_status.description:
Whether Fly.io could reach the Machine's host: `ok` if it could, `unreachable` if it
could not, in which case the response is built from last known state. `unknown` if the
host's status was not reported.

image_ref.description: The image the Machine runs, as resolved when it was last created or updated.

incomplete_config.description:
Last known configuration, returned in place of `config` when the host could not be
reached (`host_status` is not `ok`) or when listing Machines with `summary=true`. It
comes from Fly.io's replicated state rather than the host, so it may be stale or lack
fields.

lease.description:
The lease currently held on the Machine. Only returned when `include_leases=true`
was requested and a lease is held.

name.description:
Name of the Machine. Generated when not provided at creation. Names are not required
to be unique.

nonce.description:
Nonce of the lease acquired on the Machine at creation. Only returned when creating a
Machine with `lease_ttl` set. Pass it in the `fly-machine-lease-nonce` header to act on
the Machine while the lease is held.

private_ip.description: The Machine's address on the organization's private (6PN) IPv6 network.

region.description: Code of the region the Machine runs in, such as `iad`.

state.description:
Current state of the Machine, taken from the status of its most recent event. One of
`created`, `starting`, `started`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `suspending`, `suspended`,
`replacing`, `replaced`, `destroying`, `destroyed`, `failed`, `migrating`, `migrated`,
`archived`, or `pending`. See https://fly.io/docs/machines/machine-states/.

updated_at.description:
Time of the Machine's most recent event, truncated to whole seconds. The zero time
(0001-01-01T00:00:00Z) if the host could not be reached. With `summary=true`, the time
Fly.io last recorded a change to the Machine.

version.description:
Unique ID of this version of the Machine. Every update creates a new version. Pass it
as `current_version` when updating the Machine to reject the update if the Machine has
changed since this version.

id.description: Unique ID of the event (a ULID).

request.description:
Details that depend on the event type. For example, `exit` events carry the exit
code and whether the process was killed for running out of memory, and `update`
events carry the new version.

source.description:
Who triggered the event: `user` for requests to this API, `flyd` for the host's
Machine manager acting on its own (for example when a Machine exits or restarts), or
`proxy` for Fly Proxy starting and stopping Machines.

status.description:
The state the Machine moved to with this event, such as `created`, `started`, or
`stopped`. The Machine's `state` is the status of its latest event.

timestamp.description: When the event happened, in Unix milliseconds.

description.description: Description given when the lease was acquired.

expires_at.description: When the lease expires, in Unix seconds.

owner.description: Email address of the user who acquired the lease.

attached_alloc_id.description:
Always null.

Deprecated: volumes are no longer attached to Nomad allocations.

attached_machine_id.description: ID of the Machine the volume is attached to, or null if it is not attached.

auto_backup_enabled.description: Whether daily automatic snapshots are taken.

block_size.description: Size of a filesystem block, in bytes. See `blocks`.

blocks.description:
Size of the volume's filesystem, in blocks of `block_size` bytes, as last reported by a
Machine that mounted the volume. 0 if never reported, if the host could not be reached,
or with `summary=true`.

blocks_avail.description: Number of filesystem blocks available to unprivileged users. See `blocks`.

blocks_free.description:
Number of free filesystem blocks, including blocks reserved for the root user. See
`blocks`.

bytes_total.description: Size of the volume, in bytes. 0 if the host could not be reached or with `summary=true`.

bytes_used.description:
Bytes of storage the volume occupies on its host. Volumes are thinly provisioned, so this
grows as blocks are written and does not shrink when files are deleted. It is not the
filesystem's usage; use `blocks` and `blocks_free` for that. 0 if the host could not be
reached or with `summary=true`.

encrypted.description: Whether the volume is encrypted at rest.

fstype.description:
Filesystem the volume was formatted with: `ext4`, or `raw` for an unformatted block
device.

host_features.description:
Features of the volume's host. Only returned when the request sets the
`fly-include-host-features: true` header.

host_status.description:
Whether Fly.io could reach the volume's host: `ok` if it could, `unreachable` or
`unknown` if it could not, in which case host-reported fields are missing.

id.description: Unique ID of the volume, such as `vol_1234567890abcdef`.

name.description: Name of the volume. Several volumes of an app can share a name.

region.description: Code of the region the volume is in.

required_host_features.description:
Host features the volume's host was required to have; see `compute.required_host_features`
in the create request.

size_gb.description: Size of the volume, in GiB.

snapshot_retention.description: Number of days snapshots of the volume are kept.

state.description:
State of the volume, such as `creating`, `created`, `extending`, `restoring`,
`hydrating`, `scheduling_destroy`, `pending_destroy`, `destroying`, `destroyed`, or
`failed`.

type.description:
Kind of volume: `local` for regular volumes, or `cache` for volumes that hold
disposable data and support neither snapshots nor restores.

zone.description:
Identifies the host the volume is on. Volumes with different zones are on different
hosts.

cmd.description: CmdOverride is used to override the default command of the image.

depends_on.description:
DependsOn can be used to define dependencies between containers. The container will only be
started after all of its dependent conditions have been satisfied.

entrypoint.description: EntrypointOverride is used to override the default entrypoint of the image.

env.description: ExtraEnv is used to add additional environment variables to the container.

env_from.description: EnvFrom can be provided to set environment variables from machine fields.

exec.description:
Image Config overrides - these fields are used to override the image configuration.
If not provided, the image configuration will be used.
ExecOverride is used to override the default command of the image.

files.description: Files are files that will be written to the container file system.

healthchecks.description: Healthchecks determine the health of your containers. Healthchecks can use HTTP, TCP or an Exec command.

image.description: Image is the docker image to run.

name.description: Name is used to identify the container in the machine.

restart.description: Restart is used to define the restart policy for the container.

secrets.description:
Secrets can be provided at the process level to explicitly indicate which secrets should be
used for the process. If not provided, the secrets provided at the machine level will be used.

stop.description: Stop is used to define the signal and timeout for stopping the container.

user.description: UserOverride is used to override the default user of the image.

condition.description:
When the container can start: once the dependency has `started`, is `healthy`, or has
`exited_successfully`

name.description: Name of the container this one depends on

exec.description: Check that a command run in the container exits with status 0

failure_threshold.description: The number of times the check must fail before considering the container unhealthy.

grace_period.description: The time in seconds to wait after a container starts before checking its health.

http.description: Check that an HTTP request succeeds

interval.description: The time in seconds between executing the defined check.

name.description: The name of the check. Must be unique within the container.

success_threshold.description: The number of times the check must succeeed before considering the container healthy.

tcp.description: Check that a TCP connection can be opened

timeout.description: The time in seconds to wait for the check to complete.

unhealthy.description: Unhealthy policy that determines what action to take if a container is deemed unhealthy

dns_forward_rules.description: Forward DNS queries for some domains to other DNS servers

hostname.description:
Hostname of the Machine. Defaults to the Machine ID. Also added to /etc/hosts with the
Machine's 6PN address

hostname_fqdn.description: Fully qualified domain name added to /etc/hosts for `hostname`

nameservers.description: Nameservers to use instead of the default, Fly.io's private DNS server `fdaa::3`

env_var.description:
EnvVar is required and is the name of the environment variable that will be set from the
secret. It must be a valid environment variable name.

field_ref.description: FieldRef selects a field of the Machine: supports id, version, app_name, private_ip, region, image.

fly.EnvFrom.description: EnvVar defines an environment variable to be populated from a machine field, env_var

command.description: The command to run to check the health of the container (e.g. ["cat", "/tmp/healthy"])

guest_path.description:
GuestPath is the path on the machine where the file will be written and must be an absolute path.
For example: /full/path/to/file.json

image_config.description: The name of an image to use the OCI image config as the file contents.

mode.description: Mode bits used to set permissions on this file as accepted by chmod(2).

raw_value.description: The base64 encoded string of the file contents.

secret_name.description: The name of the secret that contains the base64 encoded file contents.

fly.File.description: A file that will be written to the Machine. One of RawValue or SecretName must be set.

headers.description: Additional headers to send with the request

method.description: The HTTP method to use to when making the request

path.description: The path to send the request to

port.description: The port to connect to, often the same as internal_port

scheme.description: Whether to use http or https

tls_server_name.description: If the protocol is https, the hostname to use for TLS certificate validation

tls_skip_verify.description: If the protocol is https, whether or not to verify the TLS certificate

compress.description: Compress response bodies. Defaults to true

h2_backend.description: Use HTTP/2 to talk to the Machine

headers_read_timeout.description: Seconds Fly Proxy waits for a client to send request headers. Defaults to 5

idle_timeout.description: Seconds a client connection can be idle between requests before it's closed. Defaults to 300

replay_cache.description:
Cache `fly-replay` responses from the Machine: once a client is replayed, its further
requests are replayed directly, keyed on a cookie or header, without asking the Machine again

response.description: Changes Fly Proxy makes to responses

headers.description:
Response headers to set. A string sets the header, a list of strings sets it to multiple
values, and false removes it

pristine.description: Don't let Fly Proxy add or change any response headers

path.description:
Optional absolute guest mount path. When set, the device is formatted as ext4.
Without a path, the device retains legacy raw block behavior. Contents survive
same-host restarts and path changes, but are discarded on size or mode changes,
relocation, recovery on another host, and cloning.

size_mb.description:
Fixed size of the Machine-owned cache drive in MiB. At most 51200.
With a path, at least 16 MiB is required; without a path, 0 disables the device.

grace_period.description: The time to wait after a VM starts before checking its health

headers.description: For http checks, headers to send with the request

method.description: For http checks, the HTTP method to use to when making the request

path.description: For http checks, the path to send the request to

port.description: The port to connect to, often the same as internal_port

protocol.description: For http checks, whether to use http or https

timeout.description: The maximum time a connection can take before being reported as failing its health check

tls_server_name.description: If the protocol is https, the hostname to use for TLS certificate validation

tls_skip_verify.description: For http checks with https protocol, whether or not to verify the TLS certificate

auto_destroy.description: Optional boolean telling the Machine to destroy itself once it’s complete (default false)

cache_drive.description: Beta: a cache drive attached to the Machine. This field may be removed in the future

checks.description: An optional object that defines one or more named top-level checks. The key for each check is the check name.

containers.description: Containers are a list of containers that will run in the machine, each from its own image.

env.description: An object filled with key/value pairs to be set as environment variables

files.description: Files to write into the Machine, from either a raw value or an app secret

guest.description: The resources (CPUs, memory, etc.) allocated to the Machine

init.description: Arguments for init, Fly.io's footprint inside the Machine, which controls how your own code is run

metadata.description: Key/value pairs of Machine metadata. Fly.io uses metadata internally for routing, process groups, and clusters

metrics.description: An optional metrics endpoint for Prometheus on Fly.io to scrape

mounts.description:
Persistent volumes to mount in the Machine. A Machine can mount at most one volume, which must be on
the same host. The mounted volume cannot be changed by updating the Machine

processes.description:
Multiple processes to run within this one Machine, all from the Machine's image. Unrelated to the
process groups in fly.toml, which run on separate Machines. To run processes from different
images, use containers instead

restart.description: Whether and how the Machine is restarted after its main process exits

rootfs.description:
Beta: the size of the Machine's root filesystem and whether it persists. This field may be
removed in the future

schedule.description:
Run the Machine at an interval: one of hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. The interval starts when
the Machine is created

services.description: Network services that Fly Proxy routes traffic to

spot.description: Spot pricing settings for the Machine

standbys.description:
Standbys enable a machine to be a standby for another. In the event of a hardware failure,
the standby machine will be started.

statics.description:
Static files to serve under a URL prefix. Fly Proxy routes matching requests to a file server
inside the Machine, bypassing your application's own process; the Machine must be running. The
files are read either from a path inside the Machine or from a Tigris bucket that belongs to the
app; no bucket is created for you

stop_config.description: How the Machine is shut down gracefully: the signal sent to it and how long to wait before a hard shutdown

cpu_kind.description:
Kind of CPU: shared or performance. Performance CPUs must be enabled for the organization.
Defaults to shared when `guest` is omitted

cpus.description:
Number of CPUs: 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 32, 64 or 128, up to 8 for shared and 16 for
performance CPUs unless the organization's limit is higher. Defaults to 1 when `guest` is
omitted

gpu_kind.description: No longer supported. Requests that set it are rejected

gpus.description: No longer supported. Requests that set it are rejected

host_dedication_id.description:
Place the Machine on hosts dedicated to the organization under this ID. Only available to
organizations with dedicated hosts

kernel_args.description: Extra arguments appended to the guest kernel command line

max_memory_mb.description:
Memory in MiB that the Machine's memory limit can later be raised to without a restart, using
the memory endpoints. Must be at least memory_mb and at most the per-CPU maximum. The Machine
starts with a limit of memory_mb

memory_mb.description:
Memory in MiB. Must be a multiple of 256 for shared and 1024 for performance CPUs, and
between 256 and 2048 (shared) or 2048 and 8192 (performance) per CPU. Defaults to 256 when
`guest` is omitted

required_host_features.description:
Host features the Machine's host must have, such as `storage-tier-1`. At most 16, each made
of lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Each feature must be enabled for the organization

fly.MachineHTTPHeader.description: For http checks, an array of objects with string field Name and array of strings field Values. The key/value pairs specify header and header values that will get passed with the check call.

cmd.description: Replaces the image's CMD. It's appended to the entrypoint

exec.description:
Command to run instead of the image's ENTRYPOINT and CMD. Takes precedence over entrypoint
and cmd

kernel_args.description: Currently has no effect. Use `guest.kernel_args` instead

swap_size_mb.description: Size in MiB of a swap device to give the Machine. Machines with swap cannot be suspended

https.description: Scrape over HTTPS instead of HTTP

path.description: HTTP path to scrape. Defaults to `/`

port.description: Port in the Machine to scrape metrics from

add_size_gb.description:
With automatic extension, grow the volume by this many GB at a time. Between 1 and 100.
Mutually exclusive with add_size_percent

add_size_percent.description:
AddSizePercent grows by a percentage of the current size, rounded up to GiB.
It is mutually exclusive with AddSizeGb.

encrypted.description: Whether the volume is encrypted. Set by Fly.io; ignored in requests

extend_threshold_percent.description:
Enable automatic volume extension: grow the volume when its usage exceeds this percentage.
Between 50 and 99; 0 disables it

min_add_size_gb.description: MinAddSizeGb is the minimum proportional growth in GiB (default 1).

name.description: Name of the volume. Set by Fly.io; ignored in requests

path.description: Absolute path in the Machine to mount the volume at. Required

size_gb.description: Size of the volume in GB. Set by Fly.io; ignored in requests

size_gb_limit.description:
With automatic extension, never grow the volume beyond this size in GB. At most the
organization's maximum volume size

volume.description:
ID (`vol_...`) or name of the volume to mount. Required. With a name, any unattached volume
of the app with that name in the Machine's region is used

end_port.description: Last public port of a range

force_https.description: Redirect plain HTTP requests to HTTPS

handlers.description:
How Fly Proxy handles connections before forwarding them: `tls` terminates TLS, `pg_tls`
terminates PostgreSQL TLS, `http` handles HTTP, `proxy_proto` adds a PROXY protocol header.
Without handlers, raw TCP is forwarded

port.description: Public port. Use either port, or start_port and end_port

start_port.description: First public port of a range

cmd.description: Replaces the image's CMD for this process. It's appended to the entrypoint

entrypoint.description: Replaces the image's ENTRYPOINT for this process

env.description: Environment variables for this process, in addition to the Machine's `env`

env_from.description: EnvFrom can be provided to set environment variables from machine fields.

exec.description:
Command to run instead of the image's ENTRYPOINT and CMD. Takes precedence over entrypoint
and cmd

ignore_app_secrets.description:
IgnoreAppSecrets can be set to true to ignore the secrets for the App the Machine belongs to
and only use the secrets provided at the process level. The default/legacy behavior is to use
the secrets provided at the App level.

secrets.description:
Secrets can be provided at the process level to explicitly indicate which secrets should be
used for the process. If not provided, the secrets provided at the machine level will be used.

user.description: User to run the process as, instead of the image's USER

max_retries.description: When policy is on-failure, the maximum number of times to attempt to restart the Machine before letting it stop.

policy.description:
* no - Never try to restart a Machine automatically when its main process exits, whether that’s on purpose or on a crash.
* always - Always restart a Machine automatically and never let it enter a stopped state, even when the main process exits cleanly.
* on-failure - Try up to MaxRetries times to automatically restart the Machine if it exits with a non-zero exit code. Default when no explicit policy is set, and for Machines with schedules.

fly.MachineRestart.description: The Machine restart policy defines whether and how flyd restarts a Machine after its main process exits. See https://fly.io/docs/machines/guides-examples/machine-restart-policy/.

persist.description:
Whether changes to the root filesystem are kept. `never` (default): reset on every start.
`restart`: kept across stops and restarts, reset when the Machine is updated. `always`: also
kept across updates

size_gb.description: Size of the root filesystem in GB. At most 50; 0 uses the default

env_var.description:
EnvVar is required and is the name of the environment variable that will be set from the
secret. It must be a valid environment variable name.

name.description:
Name is optional and when provided is used to reference a secret name where the EnvVar is
different from what was set as the secret name.

fly.MachineSecret.description: A Secret needing to be set in the environment of the Machine. env_var is required

autostart.description: Whether Fly Proxy starts stopped or suspended Machines when requests arrive. Defaults to true

autostop.description:
Accepts a string (new format) or a boolean (old format). For backward compatibility with older clients, the API continues to use booleans for "off" and "stop" in responses.
* "off" or false - Do not autostop the Machine.
* "stop" or true - Automatically stop the Machine.
* "suspend" - Automatically suspend the Machine, falling back to a full stop if this is not possible.

checks.description: An optional list of service checks

concurrency.description: Load limits Fly Proxy uses to balance traffic across Machines

internal_port.description: Port in the Machine that Fly Proxy forwards traffic to. Defaults to 8080

min_machines_running.description:
When autostop is on, the number of Machines Fly Proxy keeps running in the app's primary
region (`PRIMARY_REGION` env var). Machines in other regions can all be stopped

ports.description: Public ports that Fly Proxy accepts traffic on

protocol.description: Protocol: tcp or udp. Defaults to tcp

grace_period.description: The time to wait after a VM starts before checking its health

headers.description: For http checks, headers to send with the request

method.description: For http checks, the HTTP method to use to when making the request

path.description: For http checks, the path to send the request to

port.description: The port to connect to, often the same as internal_port

protocol.description: For http checks, whether to use http or https

timeout.description: The maximum time a connection can take before being reported as failing its health check

tls_server_name.description: If the protocol is https, the hostname to use for TLS certificate validation

tls_skip_verify.description: For http checks with https protocol, whether or not to verify the TLS certificate

hard_limit.description:
Fly Proxy sends no more than this many connections or requests to a Machine at once. 0 means
no hard limit

soft_limit.description:
Above this many connections or requests, Fly Proxy prefers other Machines. Defaults to 20,
and is lowered to hard_limit if higher

max_price_fraction.description: MaxPriceFraction is the maximum fraction of the full Machine price you will pay for this Machine. Range: (0, 1.0]

fly_src.description: With version v2, add the Fly-Src header and its signature to the PROXY protocol header

version.description: PROXY protocol version: v1 (default) or v2

allow_bypass.description: Let clients skip the cache by sending the `fly-replay-cache-control: skip` header

name.description: Name of the cookie or header to key the cache on

path_prefix.description:
Requests whose path starts with this prefix use the rule. May start with a hostname, e.g.
`example.com/api/*`

ttl_seconds.description: How long a cached replay is used, in seconds

guest_path.description: The path inside the Machine, or inside tigris_bucket when set, where the files to serve are located

index_document.description: The document served for requests to the URL prefix or any of its subfolders. Only works with tigris_bucket

tigris_bucket.description:
An existing Tigris bucket belonging to the app to read the files from, instead of the Machine's
filesystem. The files are still served through the Machine

url_prefix.description: The URL prefix under which the files are served

signal.description: Signal to send to the Machine's processes. Defaults to SIGINT

timeout.description:
How long to wait for the Machine to exit after sending the signal, before killing it. At most
5 minutes (1 minute for spot Machines). Defaults to 5s (60s for spot Machines)

port.description: The port to connect to, often the same as internal_port

alpn.description: ALPN protocols to offer, e.g. `h2`, `http/1.1`. Defaults to `h2` and `http/1.1`

default_self_signed.description: Use a self-signed certificate when there is no certificate for the requested hostname

versions.description: TLS versions to accept: `TLSv1.2`, `TLSv1.3`. Defaults to both

addr.description: Address and port of the DNS server to forward queries to over TCP, e.g. `10.0.0.1:53`

basename.description: Domain to forward queries for, including subdomains. Must end in a dot, e.g. `example.com.`

FlyBearerAuth.description: A Fly API token with access to the requested organization or resource. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <Fly API token>`.
